messages:
maya: Hey team — putting up an RFC + lightweight PRD draft for the embedding migration customers asked about. Core ask: change base embedding dim from 768 -> 1024 for new models while keeping rerank/lookup stable for existing vectors. Need acceptance criteria, edge-case list, and rollout plan. Short thread of items I want input on.

jonah: thanks maya. can you paste the high-level constraints? e.g., are we changing normalization semantics too, or only dim?

maya: only dim for model outputs, normalization semantics should remain L2-normalized by default. but customers asked about backward compatibility for existing indices and hybrid rerank paths.

emily: quick note: changing dim will break simple index dot-product comparators unless we pad or map dims. we should enumerate options: 1) zero-pad older vectors to 1024, 2) learn a projection, 3) reindex existing corpora. each has cost/quality tradeoffs.

jonah: agree. also need to decide batch semantics: new model has slightly different sequence-to-vector behavior under continuous batching (KV caching) — there are edge cases when generating user-provided vectors with short context. need a flag to force deterministic single-request mode for critical customers.

alejandra: from infra/SLO POV: any migration that requires reindexing at scale must include throttled background jobs, retry/backoff, and a canary path. we need rollout criteria: <1% error increase, latency p95 impact <10ms, and cost delta bounds.

patrick: implementation question: can we support runtime compatibility by returning a small header showing vector schema, e.g., `vec_dim:1024, norm:l2, version:2` so downstream can handle padding/projection? Might avoid contract break for embeddings API.

maya: yes good call. RFC should include a `schema` meta header. acceptance criteria proposal: 1) API returns schema and model_version 2) SDKs default to graceful pad->metric-aware operation 3) docs + migration guide published 4) test coverage for cross-dim scoring paths.

emily: acceptance metrics to measure: A) nearest-neighbor recall on sample corpora before/after, B) rerank MRR on benchmark queries, C) production regression alerts for any customers with tailored rerank weights. suggest thresholds: recall dip <2% absolute, MRR drop <1% relative.

jonah: edge cases to add: - mixed-batch inference where one request uses 768 vectors and another 1024 in the same micro-batch; - KV cache reuse when model variant changes mid-session; - embeddings stored with custom normalization (customers who set norm:false). For mixed-batch, we should reject or convert at router layer rather than letting runtime mishandle shapes.

maya: for mixed-batch: RFC suggests that router normalizes batches by target model dim. if mismatch, attempt conversion (pad or project). if conversion costs exceed threshold, route serially with code 429-like hint for client to retry with explicit dims.

patrick: technical note: projecting 768->1024 requires learned matrix or random init + orthonormalization. doing online projection for billions of vectors is expensive. prefer padding + recalibrated scoring unless customers require quality. we should include a config knob: `compat_projection: on|off` for Dedicated/Private.

alejandra: logging: emit a per-customer metric when we trigger conversion or serial routing. also add an alert when conversions >0.1% of requests for 24h. we can gate on that for rollback.

emily: test matrix: small scale QA with seeded corpora (3 customers), synthetic mixed batches, and long-tail fuzzing of normalization flags. add unit tests for scoring code with: `dot(pad(u),v)`, `cosine(project(u),v)`, and make sure numerical stability is OK for p95 token latency.

jonah: draft of acceptance criteria (short): - Schema header present and stable. - No silent shape errors in router or runtime. - Cross-dim scoring implemented (pad+score) and tested. - Migration guide + SDK helpers published. - Canary metrics within thresholds (recall, MRR, latency).

maya: cool. last piece: launch plan. propose phases: alpha (internal + 2 opt-in customers) -> beta (broad opt-in) -> GA (default). gating for GA: fewer than 3 customers with active conversions >0.1% and no MRR regressions. MVP for alpha should allow padding only. projection reserved for beta if customers opt-in.

jonah: small code snippet for pad scoring to include in RFC:```
# pad to target_dim
def pad(vec, target_dim):
    if len(vec) >= target_dim: return vec[:target_dim]
    return np.concatenate([vec, np.zeros(target_dim - len(vec))])

# dot-score
def score(q, doc):
    q_p = pad(q, 1024)
    d_p = pad(doc, 1024)
    return np.dot(q_p, d_p)
```

maya: perfect. I'll fold this into the RFC doc and add proposed SLO thresholds and the canary metric list. Please comment inline in the doc (link to draft coming in #eng-ml). thanks :thumbsup:

mira-bot: RFC draft created: /docs/rfcs/embed-compat-1765509012.md — reviewers: jonah, emily, alejandra, patrick.
